articles.title: EU backs cross-border CO2 transport and storage project with €223 million
articles.summary: Aker BP and Höegh Evi have secured €223 million from the European Union Innovation Fund for a large-scale CO2 transport and storage (CCS) project...
articles.body: Carbon Capture Usage & Storage October 20, 2026 · 15 hours ago EU backs cross-border CO2 transport and storage project with €223 million NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Aker BP Aker BP and Höegh Evi have secured €223 million from the European Union Innovation Fund for a large-scale CO2 transport and storage (CCS) project that will permanently store CO2 on the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS) from European industry. The Atlas project, which combines regional CO2 aggregation, large-scale low-pressure maritime transport and offshore storage, has a design capacity of 6 million tons of CO2 per year, with potential to expand beyond 10 million tons as the European CCS market develops. Confirmed as an EU Project of Mutual Interest (PMI 13.17) this April, being recognized as cross-border European CO2 infrastructure, the project has completed the feasibility phase and progressed into the Select phase, targeting a final investment decision (FID) in 2028 and first injection from 2031. "Atlas demonstrates how regional aggregation and large-scale low-pressure shipping can efficiently connect industrial regions to permanent CO₂ storage. This flexible maritime model can expand as the European CCS market develops," said Nils Jakob Hasle , EVP Clean Energy at Höegh Evi. According to Höegh Evi, CO2 will be aggregated at regional export hubs close to industrial clusters and transported by dedicated carriers to the Atlas storage site in the Norwegian North Sea. The CO2 will be injected through subsea infrastructure into a saline aquifer for storage more than 2,000 meters below the seabed at the storage site located in the Aker BP-operated EXL011 (80% Aker BP, 20% ORLEN Upstream Norway). "Europe needs safe and cost-effective permanent CO₂ storage. Atlas is designed to provide European industries with significant storage capacity on the Norwegian Continental Shelf and capture economies of scale needed to reduce CCS value chain costs," said Ørjan Jentoft , CCS Asset Manager at Aker BP. articles.body: Environment Europe Operations Regulatory UK shipowners warn against copying FuelEU red tape Adis Ajdin October 20, 2026 0 226 1 minute read UK Government UK Government The UK Chamber of Shipping has urged the British government to avoid repeating the compliance problems encountered under FuelEU Maritime as it prepares to introduce its own maritime fuel standard. In a policy paper published this week, the industry body warned that the EU regime, which came into force in January 2025, had imposed a substantially greater administrative workload on shipowners and regulators than initially anticipated. The 22-page report identifies difficulties with reporting deadlines, fuel certification, emissions calculations and compliance pooling arrangements. Some operators missed deadlines despite meeting their operational obligations, while inconsistencies between verification systems created additional work. The Chamber wants the UK government to establish a fully tested ship-level monitoring and reporting system before introducing compliance obligations. It is also pushing for fuel-neutral regulation, realistic emissions targets based on fuel availability and infrastructure readiness, and flexibility for owners and operators to meet their obligations without unnecessary commercial disruption. Peter Aylott, the Chamber’s director of policy, said the government had an opportunity to learn from the EU’s experience rather than create another regulatory system that increased costs and complexity. The paper also calls for close alignment with emerging International Maritime Organization requirements to avoid duplicate certification, reporting and verification obligations. The intervention comes as the Department for Transport prepares to consult on a domestic maritime fuel standard, with the consultation expected later this year. Britain’s maritime decarbonisation strategy, unveiled in March 2025, targets a 30% reduction in domestic shipping’s lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions by 2030, rising to 80% by 2040 and zero by 2050, against a 2008 baseline. The government has identified fuel regulation and emissions pricing as central measures for meeting those targets. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 3 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Illustration Source: Sunda Energy, former Baron Oil SundaGas Banda Unipessoal, a wholly owned subsidiary of the UK-based and AIM-listed Sunda Energy, has dodged a bullet in Timor-Leste with a crucial 12-month reprieve, since the regulatory extension keeps hopes alive for the long-awaited appraisal well following a termination warning earlier this year over missed deadlines, as partner negotiations heat up. Sunda Energy’s subsidiary has received from Autoridade Nacional do Petróleo (ANP), Timor-Leste’s upstream regulator, an extension of 12 months to the current phase of the production sharing contract (PSC) TL-SO-19-16, which contains the Chuditch gas field, where SundaGas has been preparing to drill the Chuditch-2 appraisal well. The firm operates this asset in partnership with its government-owned joint venture partner, Timor Gap Chuditch Unipessoal . The operator disclosed in June 2026 the receipt of a letter of notice of intention to terminate the PSC from ANP, stating that the joint venture was in breach, having failed to fulfill the minimum exploration work requirements for the third year of the PSC contract, regarding the drilling of the Chuditch-2 well by June 18, 2026. The notice gave the joint venture 120 days to submit written representations to ANP, following which it may terminate the PSC. These talks are ongoing and include, among other things, a farm-in by Timor Gap for an enlarged working interest in the PSC and the transfer of operatorship to the other firm. The extension granted by ANP allows the joint venture time to continue the discussions, with a stated timeline for completion prior to the end of 2026. Sunda explains that this extension is subject to a suspension of the uplift on the cost recovery account for the PSC from June 19, 2024, until such time as drilling operations on Chuditch-2 have started. This extension is an important milestone as we progress towards the drilling of Chuditch-2.” Related Articles Fossil Energy Southeast Asian oil field development clears key environmental hurdle to move toward FID 2 min read Meanwhile, the company notes that Finder Energy revealed on October 15, 2026, the signing of a contract for a drilling rig for the Kuda Tasi and Jahal (KTJ) development in Timor-Leste, with the rig having additional optional drilling slots that provide flexibility to accommodate participation by other operators. The firm is continuing to liaise with Finder under the framework of the letter of intent announced in April 2026 with respect to collaboration between the planned drilling campaigns for KTJ and Chuditch-2 drilling campaigns. This extension in Timor-Leste comes shortly after Sunda Energy revealed progress made in New Zealand , securing exclusive rights to advance its petroleum exploration permit application over the decades-old gas-condensate field in the offshore Taranaki Basin. articles.body: Europe Finance and Insurance Tankers Marinakis tanker venture locks down $930m for 11 VLCC newbuilds Adis Ajdin October 20, 2026 0 1,253 1 minute read Capital Group Capital Group Greek shipowner Capital Tankers has lined up $930.3m in financing for 11 VLCC newbuildings under construction in China and South Korea, making further headway in funding its expanding crude tanker fleet. The Evangelos Marinakis-backed company has signed four financing arrangements since late September, covering vessels booked at Hanwha Ocean, Dalian Shipbuilding Industry Co (DSIC) and Hengli Shipbuilding. The largest portion, totalling $450.6m, covers five 307,000 dwt VLCCs at DSIC. Three vessels are being financed at between $89.6m and $90.9m each under an October agreement, with another two securing $89.6m apiece. Capital Tankers has also arranged $241.8m for three 320,000 dwt LNG dual-fuel-ready VLCCs at South Korea’s Hanwha Ocean, alongside $237.9m for three 306,000 dwt vessels at Hengli in China. The Hanwha financing carries a five-year repayment schedule, while the Chinese yard packages are structured over ten years. All include substantial balloon payments at maturity, ranging from $39.7m to $60.9m per vessel. The company has not identified the financing providers. Separately, Capital Tankers has disclosed a $64.5m sale-and-leaseback arrangement for its newly delivered 155,348 dwt LNG dual-fuel suezmax Amor , built at New Times Shipbuilding in China. The financing, arranged earlier this year, runs to October 2033, with a $40m final payment. The latest financing commitments follow Capital Tankers’ $500m Oslo private placement earlier this year, which was upsized after strong investor demand as the Marinakis group brought its crude tanker business to the public market. The owner has since continued adding tonnage. In June, it acquired three VLCC newbuilding contracts at Hengli from parent Capital Maritime & Trading at $122m apiece, with deliveries scheduled for the second half of 2027. Capital Tankers now controls a 33-vessel fleet comprising 15 VLCCs, 10 suezmaxes and eight aframax/LR2 tankers. Seventeen vessels are trading, with another 16 due for delivery through mid-2028. The company also retains options for 13 additional crude tankers. articles.body: Containers Europe Euroseas seals bumper charter and $26m boxship sale Adis Ajdin October 20, 2026 0 410 1 minute read Euroseas Euroseas Nasdaq-listed Greek containership owner Euroseas has secured a $62,500-a-day charter for a 25-year-old feeder vessel while agreeing to sell its sistership for $26m, capitalising on continued strength in the smaller boxship market. The Aristides Pittas-led company said its 2001-built, 2,556 teu EM Corfu has been fixed for a minimum of 12 and maximum of 14 months at the charterer’s option. The new contract will begin in mid-December, following a scheduled drydocking, and represents a sharp increase from the vessel’s previous employment at $28,000 per day. Euroseas expects the minimum charter period to generate approximately $17.8m in EBITDA. The company has also agreed to sell the 2001-built, 2,556 teu Evridiki G to an unrelated third party for approximately $26m. The vessel is expected to change hands at the end of October, once its current charter expires. Euroseas anticipates recording an accounting gain of approximately $22.5m from the disposal. Both vessels were previously fixed in November 2024, with EM Corfu securing $28,000 per day and Evridiki G $29,500 per day. The latest charter more than doubles EM Corfu’s previous daily rate, while the sale allows Euroseas to realise a substantial gain from its sistership without undertaking another costly drydocking. Following the disposal, Euroseas will operate 20 containerships with a combined capacity of approximately 58,600 teu. The company also has 12 vessels under construction in China, ranging from 1,800 teu feeders to 4,484 teu intermediate containerships, with deliveries scheduled between 2027 and 2029. articles.body: Dry Cargo Europe Operations Dutch inland shipping duo expands into Belgium with new chartering venture Adis Ajdin October 20, 2026 0 590 1 minute read TriBarge TriBarge Dutch inland shipping companies Amer Shipping and Van de Graaf & Meeusen have joined forces to establish a new chartering business in Antwerp, backed by a fresh dry cargo newbuilding order at Concordia Damen. The two family-owned operators have launched TriBarge to target Belgian and French shippers, combining their existing networks and vessel capacity with plans for joint fleet investment. The new company will handle dry cargo, general cargo and breakbulk movements across the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) region, German canals, the Moselle and inland waterways reaching Basel. Through its partnership with Stream Shipping, an existing venture between Amer Shipping and German cooperative MSG eG, TriBarge will also be able to serve destinations as far as the Black Sea. The partners have already contracted an 85 m dry cargo vessel at Concordia Damen. The newbuilding, to be named Porta Sud , is scheduled to enter service in the second half of 2027 and will be designed to access smaller inland ports, tributaries and canals as well as major rivers. The move comes just weeks after Amer Shipping returned to Concordia Damen for another two 110 m CDS Dry Cargo newbuildings, lifting its programme of shallow-draught vessels to six. Those ships are scheduled for delivery in the fourth quarter of 2027 and the second quarter of 2028. The first, AM Lianova , will join Stream Shipping, while the second will enter Amer’s own fleet. Amer Shipping operates a network of close to 60 vessels, transporting around 9m tonnes of cargo annually across the Netherlands, Belgium, France, Germany and Switzerland. Its new partner, Van de Graaf & Meeusen, is a Ridderkerk-based inland shipping and chartering specialist with a fleet of pushboats and barges serving the dry bulk market. TriBarge will operate from Antwerp’s Tweede Havendok, with Devin van Dam joining as a chartering broker on November 1. Another Belgian broker is expected to join in the second quarter of 2027.
